attachments.origin_landmark: flexor retinaculum and the ulnar border of the palmar aponeurosis
attachments.insertion_landmark: skin of the ulnar border of the palm

innervation.root_levels: C8-T1 (superficial branch of the ulnar nerve)

actions: wrinkles the skin of the hypothenar eminence, deepening the palmar hollow for grip

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: The only muscle in the hand that inserts entirely into skin. It covers Guyon's canal, and its preserved function in an ulnar lesion at the wrist -- the palmaris brevis sign -- helps localise the level of injury.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

clinical.compiled_by: repository owner (physician); hand_intrinsic_muscles_reference_v1.html, compiled 03/09/2026. Source hierarchy used. (1) Peer-reviewed anatomical and biomechanical studies (bibliographic data and abstracts retrieved via PubMed/NCBI, 01–03/09/2026; DOIs linked in the reference list); (2) reference textbooks — Standring (Gray's Anatomy, 42nd ed., 2021), Kapandji (2007), Green's Operative Hand Surgery (8th ed., 2022), Brand & Hollister (1999); (3) Simons, Travell & Simons, The Trigger Point Manual Vol. 1, 2nd ed. (1999) and 3rd ed. (2019) for trigger-point (TrP) referral patterns; (4) StatPearls/NCBI Bookshelf for cross-checking. No item below relies on blogs or unattributed aggregators; where secondary TrP summaries were used to confirm Travell & Simons figures, they are graded accordingly in the verification table.
clinical.function_biomechanics: Corrugates the hypothenar skin, deepens the palmar cup and improves purchase while padding the ulnar neurovascular bundle during grip; it co-contracts with D5 abduction [1][20]. Its diagnostic value exceeds its mechanics: sparing of PB in an intrinsic ulnar palsy places the lesion in the deep branch (zone 2) distal to the superficial-branch origin — the "palmaris brevis sign" derived directly from the zonal anatomy of Gross & Gelberman [29]. Involuntary hypothenar dimpling ("palmaris brevis spasm syndrome") is a rare, benign case-report entity worth recognising to avoid over-investigation.
clinical.adjacent_structures: Relations: Forms part of the roof over the distal ulnar tunnel, lying directly on the ulnar artery and superficial branch — a fleshy shield over Guyon's canal outlet [1][5][29].

trigger_points.referred_pain: Not described in Travell & Simons; symptomatic TrPs are not an established entity for this muscle — local hypothenar skin discomfort should redirect attention to ADM/ODM, Guyon structures and the ulnar artery [24][29].

pain_referred_into_this_muscle_from: Same ulnar-hand list as ADM; superficial "prickling palm" pain specifically suggests palmaris longus TrPs [24].
clinical.caveat: Most myofascial hand pain is imported: shoulder-girdle, arm and forearm TrPs project distally far more often than intrinsic TrPs project proximally. Patterns below are the prototype maps of Simons, Travell & Simons (Vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1999; 3rd ed., 2019) — screening guides, not fingerprints; individual spread is wide [24][25]. Non-myofascial mimics are listed per zone for the same working position [5][29][31][35]. TrP → = habitual referred-pain direction of that muscle's trigger points (Simons, Travell & Simons 1999/2019); patterns are prototypes — individual variation is wide.
